facts.text: The repository is titled Integrate_Microscope_eeDAP
The README says the rough drafts were written while creating the hardware control for the Prior ProScan III controller
The README's folder structure places proscan.py in hardware_control/prior_stage/ and base_stage.py in hardware_control/
The README says PriorStage talks to the ProScan III controller through PySerial in messages composed of bytes and points at section 4 of the controller manual
The README says move_to accepts xy coordinates in JSON format and converts them to the byte string the controller understands
The README says its instructions run the test script in Python 3.8.10 in a virtual environment
BaseStage is an abstract class whose only abstract methods are move_to(delta) and close()
base_stage.py says BaseStage is based on the OpenFlexure base stage class and the Python-Microscope ProScanIII class
proscan.py appends the parent of its own folder to sys.path and then imports BaseStage from a top-level base_stage module
proscan.py says _PriorConnection is based on the _ProScanIII connection of Python-Microscope
proscan.py says PriorStage is also based on the _ProScanIII class of Python-Microscope and inspired by its Stage class
PriorStage extends BaseStage and creates a _PriorConnection from the port in __init__
The serial connection is opened at 9600 baud with eight data bits, one stop bit, no parity, xonxoff, rtscts and dsrdtr off and timeout=3
The connection handshake writes '?' and requires the reply 'PROSCAN INFORMATION\r', then reads until '\rEND\r'
A connection write appends a carriage return to the data
validate_response writes a command, reads one reply with the serial timeout raised to ten times its value and prints the reply
When the reply matches no expected response, validate_response prints a meaning for the replies E,1 to E,5 and E,8, calls read_until_timeout() and raises RuntimeError
move_to reads x and y from the mapping, writes str() of each into b'G ' + x + b',' + y, prints the goal and passes the command to validate_response expecting b'R\r'
A None x or y raises MissingCoordinate, which move_to catches and only prints
The PriorStage class defines only __init__, move_to and close; it has no position query, stop, halt or abort method
close() calls the connection's close() and prints 'Successfully closed'; a bare except only prints that the serial port cannot be closed
The example test script is run as 'python move_stage_tester.py' and imports PriorStage from a top-level proscan module
The example test script opens PriorStage('COM4'), calls move_to with -100000 and 100000 and then close()
The Flask app constructs PriorStage('COM4') and moves to (-100000, -100000) and then (100000, 100000) on a request to /stage_test, and runs with debug=True on host 0.0.0.0
The Dockerfile copies app.py, proscan.py, base_stage.py and check_ports.py into the image root and runs app.py
The upstream requirements list pyserial==3.5
The Micro-Manager configuration names a Prior XYStage on port COM4 with BaudRate 9600 and AnswerTimeout 500.0000

estop.terminal: Upstream: PriorStage.close() only closes the serial port and sends no stop command (proscan.py:180-186), and only constructing a new PriorStage opens a port (proscan.py:147-150, 25-36). Package policy: this driver never reopens the port inside an endpoint, so a new endpoint, which repeats the connection handshake (proscan.py:40-56), is the only recovery. A move already sent is not stopped; the clone has no stop, abort or position query.
